notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Black-and-white striped signposts, sometimes black-and-yellow; the only South American country to use them.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Black-and-yellow striped guardrails; the neighbour to the southeast has similar ones but with a yellow outer stripe.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Red or yellow painted bollards, mostly triangular concrete ones, sometimes circular.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Metal signposts have a concrete block at the bottom; no other South American country does this.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: White plates, plus yellow ones less often; taxis have yellow on top and white below.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Generation 3 is a solid black or white car.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Has Generation 4 and smallcam coverage, unlike its southeastern neighbour.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: White edge lines always; highways have single dashed or double yellow centres, rural mountain roads often have no centre line.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Concrete kilometre markers painted black and white.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Concrete or wooden poles, some with horizontal concrete bars.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles often have a painted base in black or black and yellow.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Bridges are commonly painted orange.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Three-wheeled mototaxis are everywhere in big cities.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Wide red and white stickers on the sides of taxis and commercial vehicles.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Rectangular metal electricity counters with two or three horizontal slits.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: The currency is the sol, with the symbol S/.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Political party logos are painted on walls everywhere and are unique to the country.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Mostly semi-arid mountain ranges and valleys; dry desert in the west, rainforest in the east.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Sandy soil with green or withered bushes along offroads in Tumbes.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Dry, low shrubby land in Piura, mostly flat with occasional rolling hills.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Flat high-mountain land around central Puno and Lake Chinchaycocha can look like Bolivia.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Barren flat desert around Ica, Arequipa and Tacna resembles northern Chile.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Dark red-tinted soil around Cusco, Ayacucho, Cajamarca and Tarapoto.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Light green lichen on rocks and ground in high central and southern areas.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Sugar cane is concentrated on the northern coast near Chiclayo and Trujillo.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Olive plantations in far southern Tacna.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Red brick buildings become more common near Lake Titicaca, like in western Bolivia.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Overhanging roofs with wooden supports, sometimes brightly coloured, in the north.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Pole markings with yellow vertical numbers are common on the northern coast and in Tacna.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Lamp posts in the capital region have a sweeping inverted J curve at the top.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: A cylindrical bollard with a black and yellow stripe at the top is unique to Moquegua.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Volcanoes are seen around Arequipa and only in the southeast.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Iquitos is isolated in the Amazon with only Generation 3, tuk-tuks and overcast skies.
